newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up sharply on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up sharply on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up sharply in active trading on Wednesday due to overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active March 1997 contract ended at 21,280 yuan ($2,563) per tonne, rising 320 yuan. It opened at 21,200 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 20,350 and a high of 21,390.
December rose 230 to 20,700, January 200 to 21,000, February 330 to 21,250, April 290 to 21,250, May 290 to 21,260 and June 270 to 21,250.
Combined volume rose to 148,600 tonnes from 110,720.
Copper opened higher and climbed further, encouraged by overnight gains on LME before profit-taking pushed prices off highs late in the session.
"LME gains boosted the confidence of long position holders in Shanghai, leading to much follow-up buying," one trader said.
"Heavy volume, with most contracts breaching the key 21,000-yuan level, indicated further rises are likely," he added.
But some traders said investors were wary about the future trend after successive days of heavy gains.
"Many investors felt that the risks are increasing along with their gains and some liquidated their long positions at high levels today," a second trader said.
Analysts expect copper to meet strong resistance at the 21,500-yuan level in the next few days.
Aluminium ended up following copper's trend. December rose 150 to 13,700 yuan per tonne, January 220 to 14,000 and February 200 to 14,150. Combined volume rose to 920 tonnes from 250.
